# Paper statement inventory · `reg:inventory:overview`

**Setup (Scope)** · `setup:inventory:scope` The inventory contains 1772 statement rows and 2833 constant entries. The paper release is network-v0.37.5. The inventory covers explicit labels and labels generated by structure and frontier environments at this release; the two censuses are separate. Each refresh re-reads every inventory row against the new release and rewrites current_at to that release; it records the text reflected by the row, not when the row was introduced. The constants field refreshed_at likewise identifies its projection edition. The inventory distinguishes 1738 explicit labels and 34 environment-generated labels; neither census silently substitutes for the other. The exact-label material_class records the paper’s closure, oracle or courtesy class independently of repository conformance classification; pure mathematics belongs to closure at this tag. Implementation kinds and proposed homes are engineering classifications, not claims that code exists or that a paper question is settled. The decomposition is recorded in (`rec:decomposition:decision`). A kind or home of none assigns no new implementation item or no Layer 1 home, respectively; documentation can still have an owner.

**Convention (Label presentation)** · `conv:inventory:labels` Paper labels are exhibited with doubled delimiters because the imported registry format is unavailable under the repository namespace. The citable field preserves eligibility under the adopted kind relation for a project-neutral import format; it does not claim that an import is active. Paper label kinds remain unchanged. Environment text is the inventory's recorded description, while implementation kind describes a proposed code responsibility. Short subdivision rows locate separately labelled cases, conditions and steps; their titles do not replace the normative statement or supply its premises.

| 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-numeraire`` | condition | Divide each frame-denominated input by the positive numeraire before combining it with a count. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-measurement`` | condition | Compute standing as a measurement of the record, not a possessed ledger asset; the ledger after measurement must equal the ledger before it. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-conservation`` | condition | Conserve full balance and count totals through row-stochastic allocation; this is rival allocation, not invariance of individual standings, participant maxima or unweighted sums. | 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-epoch-set`` | condition | Keep host-assigned order, relation frontiers and intra-epoch latest positions out of every standing quantity. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-title`` | condition | Resolve settlement counterparty allocation through structurally completed branch events, independently of terminal timeline selection. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-memorylessness`` | condition | Use no previous epoch’s standing as a semantic input. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-universal-act-weighing`` | condition | Weigh every accepted Actor-authored act exactly once, resolving to a person or self; consume matched hyper-acts atomically so unmatched legs and passive artifacts carry no standing. Admissible partitions can change author-indexed folds and normalized allocation, so invariance needs additional premises. The all-state hop-intertwining premises of ``thm:dynamics:split-hop-refinement`` are a sufficient invariance criterion, not a consequence of act partition alone. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-domain-weights`` | condition | Apply declared domain weights to complete folded acts; preserving aggregate ledger pairs does not by itself preserve the resulting author-indexed allocation. The all-state hop-intertwining premises of ``thm:dynamics:split-hop-refinement`` are a sufficient invariance criterion, not a consequence of act partition alone. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-responsive-tilt`` | condition | Use recipient standing only to modulate relative authored allocation, with hop fading at the greatest certified rung. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-cluster-rate`` | condition | Preserve the closed transported-count-weighted mean under internal pair allocation; neither an open fibre mean nor individual coordinates or maxima are thereby fixed. | 02 Comparator | ``cond:comparator:faithfulness-complete-set-admission`` | condition | Require complete-set admission to read only the completed post-debit standing result; this is a boundary-operator obligation, not a consequence of the standing construction. | 02 Comparator | ``ins:comparator:universal-amplifier`` | insight | Terminal value channels use dimensionless standing amplification without manufacturing source. | 02 Comparator | ``rem:comparator:amplifier-rendering`` | remark | Terminal amplification must not silently become an admission-policy control. These are separate fixtures, not a claim that every ledger has every effect. There is also a depleted-source frame gross comparison with a decreasing reached recipient at the anchor. For selected rungs there is no finite universal upper bound on standing loss divided by a positive frame gross increment. One additional accepted act without additional frame gross amount has no universal direction; in the ordinary regime without an additional finite source ceiling its absolute own-standing loss is unbounded across admissible ledgers even when both contributing widths are zero. The fixed-rung losses in the certified fixtures are small in absolute size; the own feedback can nevertheless exceed the source actor's own direct forcing. One act can remove a substantial fraction of an isolated Actor's standing. The bounds are ``prop:epoch:frame-gross-response-bound``, ``prop:epoch:finite-standing-response``; the surviving positive regimes are ``cor:epoch:frame-gross-monotone-regimes``. | A Gates | ``app:gates`` | appendix | Track gates as a separately addressable appendix. | closure | none | pn-verification | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``rem:gates:split-scope`` | remark | For an unsupported Actor sustaining reduced rate c, each accepted act requires c times numeraire plus the action price in new frame gross amount; wall-neutral sustaining frame gross amount is twice that price. Relational support may help stamps but never reduces the own-balance debit. Additional Registration debit and incremental aggregate frame gross amount are distinct, and cost alone bounds no small standing gain. Use the separate Registration-debit and incremental aggregate frame gross amount denominators of ``prop:epoch:split-registration-cost``. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``subsec:gates:door-and-wall`` | subsection | Track door and wall as a separately addressable subsection. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | False | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``thm:gates:sustaining`` | theorem | An unendorsed Actor preserving reduced own rate c across an accepted act needs exactly c times the numeraire plus the action price in new frame gross amount. At the safety wall this is twice the price; at the door it is the door rate's frame image plus the debit. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``cor:gates:band-floor`` | corollary | Check that unsupported wall-neutral activity needs twice the action threshold. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``rem:gates:propped`` | remark | Never let relational standing pay another actor's solvency debit. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``subsec:gates:frontier`` | subsection | Track frontier as a separately addressable subsection. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | False | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``thm:gates:frontier`` | theorem | Check the unsupported long-run sustaining lower bounds under their fixed-floor premises. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``prop:gates:two-phase-transit`` | proposition | For an unendorsed Actor acting without new frame amount, the stated exact action-count formulas give door and safety-wall crossing and band dwell, subject to headroom. Re-entry needs additional amount, not elapsed time. These own-source formulas do not predict a relational stamp without replaying its standing package. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``rem:gates:frontload`` | remark | Front-loading supplied frame amount can delay an unendorsed Actor's door or wall crossing without lowering its long-run own-source sustaining average. Acquisition timing and price lie below Layer 1; relational standing can alter stamps but not the own-balance debit. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``subsec:gates:lever`` | subsection | Track lever as a separately addressable subsection. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | False | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``cor:gates:standing-transport-no-solvency-discount`` | corollary | Keep every accepted actor's own threshold debit unchanged by transport. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``rem:gates:tilt-is-not-price-discount`` | remark | Lowering responsiveness does not alter the debit, numeraire or policy floor. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``thm:gates:equal-rate-no-internal-lift`` | theorem | When every contributing pair, including the own pair, has one common reduced rate, computed reduced standing equals that rate under every certified allocation. This exact invariance does not extend to heterogeneous funded partitions. The receiving-family concentration of ``prop:epoch:split-concentration`` remains compatible with these scoped invariants. | closure | invariant check | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``rem:gates:external`` | remark | Bound relational assistance by contributing source rates rather than a fixed discount. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``subsec:gates:funding`` | subsection | Track funding as a separately addressable subsection. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | False | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``rem:gates:guild-funding`` | remark | Supplied funding retains its opaque Actor attribution. Additional amount can change residual balance, but standing and terminal effects require their separate response and fixed-context comparisons; funding neither freezes allocation nor chooses an uncertified rung. Funded partitions still pay each Registration debit even when matched histories have zero aggregate frame increment. | closure | policy | pn-records | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``rem:gates:standing-safety-scope`` | remark | Separate own-balance solvency, individual and epoch gates, contraction and movement; conserve transported pairs without transferring ledger assets. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| A Gates | ``rem:gates:sustaining-denomination`` | remark | Keep the numeraire conversion, literal action debit, policy membrane, safety wall and tilt rung distinct. The sustaining amount is reduced own rate times numeraire plus debit; changing any one dial is not a generic cheaper action. | closure | policy | pn-epoch | True | network-v0.37.5; explicit |

The mechanism owes agreement, selection and availability; optional exact reuse owes equality and measured benefit. Richer terminal sign transport is governed by the guild grant and formula completeness, not an architectural frontier. Four architectural extensions leave no Layer-1 open problem. | closure | policy | pn-replay | False | network-v0.37.5; explicit |
| G Frontiers | ``frontier:boundary-mechanism`` | frontier (arch) | Specify the submission model, candidate class, assumptions and testable selection guarantee. Establish agreement on the published act sequence, placement, causally closed edge set and complete calculation package; recompute logical time rather than agree it. Search policy, budgets and fallback concern conduct, and no timeout permits an invalid accepted set. External wall-clock measurement audits published durations; the asserted timestamp verifies no elapsed time. Written-side accountability proves neither treatment of unwritten candidates nor decentralized selection. | closure | policy | pn-host | False | network-v0.37.5; environment |

## Constants · `sec:inventory:constants`

**Observation (Source definitions)** · `obs:inventory:constants` Empty class and citation fields preserve absence in the released collection. The dataset retains source literal strings, expressions, function selectors and display rules in its definition field; a function selector is not an evaluated numeric result or a certificate. It contains 2830 declarations and the separate standing_profile, verification_fixtures and act_time_fixture records. The verification profile retains the published exact inputs, precision and comparison settings for the released finite witnesses; their scope is the declared fixtures, not a universal performance or economic claim. The standing profile preserves exact rational strings for hop shape, depth masses, self-retention and certified strength, plus the domain-weight mode, grounding the reference case in ``ver:standing:conserved-equilibrium-enclosure``. The act-time fixture retains ordered acts, epochs, incidence, public parents, opened dependencies and published stamps for ``ver:boundary:act-time-recomputation``. Its result selectors name exact integer replay results; they are not substituted evaluated values. The input schema is peer-constants-2; the added profile does not imply that old readers understand its additional member. Generated decimal displays alone supply no numerical proof.

**Model (Reference standing profile)** · `model:inventory:standing-profile` The exact hop shape is 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, the normalized depth masses are 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8, self-retention is 1, domain weighting is uniform_unit, and certified strength is 1. No intermediate rung grid is inferred from this reference declaration; deployment grids remain separate.

**Open Question (Bridge reaction placement)** · `open:inventory:bridge-reaction-placement` Owner: the deploying operator for the published centralized-phase reaction, and the repository architecture reviewer, the role that reviews scope and crate-responsibility changes for repository acceptance, for resolving the implementation boundary. ``case:transport:bridge-eligibility-cliff`` requires the threshold, share-volatility companion and conditional reference-rule publication; ``rem:bridge:eligibility-cliff-primary`` makes flip frequency a distribution-stability measure. The existing responsibility map gives pn-readouts published standing/title and optional raw views, and pn-host package publication, while placing bridge computation, guild policy and CAN outside the implementation (`conv:design:scope`), (`rec:decomposition:decision`). It does not assign computation of bridge selection and normalized-share history, so neither crate is inferred as owner. Settle the question either through a deployment-owned computation over published epoch certificates, recording its metric and publication contract, or through an accepted scope amendment assigning that computation and contract to a crate; until then these rows retain kind policy and no crate. The publication obligation is required even though adopting its terminal reference rule remains optional.

**Open Question (Deployment terminal evidence placement)** · `open:inventory:deployment-terminal-evidence` Owner: the deploying operator for terminal consumers and their published measurements, and the repository architecture reviewer, the role reviewing scope and crate-responsibility changes, for any implementation assignment. The optional cadence/maturity, payload/cache and terminal-regression scopes of ``cond:deployment:cadence-maturity``, ``cond:deployment:payload-cache-envelope`` and ``cond:deployment:terminal-regression`` include CAN, bridge or application measurements outside (`conv:design:scope`). Existing bites supply canonical epoch certificates, optional raw service and conformance inputs, but do not assign those consumers or cache deployments to a crate. No monitoring standard is adopted. Settle any future undertaking by a deployment-owned measurement contract over published outputs, or by an accepted scope amendment assigning its implementation; these inventory rows assign no new crate or bite. Local finite comparisons remain usable without a courtesy-standard claim. realizes{``cond:deployment:cadence-maturity``; This scope hold names unassigned publication and comparison duties without asserting measured terminal performance.} realizes{``cond:deployment:payload-cache-envelope``; This scope hold names unassigned publication and comparison duties without asserting measured terminal performance.} realizes{``cond:deployment:terminal-regression``; This scope hold names unassigned publication and comparison duties without asserting measured terminal performance.}

**Convention (Deployment inventory scope)** · `conv:inventory:deployment-scope` The deployment rows retain the paper's statements without asserting their external premises. Their repository conformance classification and declared conditional dependencies are the generated tables of (`rule:testing:public-record-conformance`); proposed homes and citation status supply no witness of hardware, availability, elapsed time or private search effort.
